nahhas-irab:1-1.t: يُسَبِّحُ لِلَّهِ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ: this may be the end of the statement, or it may be connected, and لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ would then be "[that which is in the heavens] belongs to Him", or لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ may be in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial); that is, His authority, His command and His decree are carried out in both of them. وَهُوَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ: that is, possessed of power over whatever He wills: He creates what He wills, gives life and causes death, exalts and abases; nothing is beyond Him, because He is the possessor of perfect power.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: هُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ: if you wish, you may assimilate the qāf into the kāf. فَمِنْكُمْ كافِرٌ وَمِنْكُمْ مُؤْمِنٌ: that is, one who affirms, certain that He is his Creator and his God and that he has no god but Him. وَاللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ: that is, knowing your deeds, so do not go against His command and His prohibition, lest He assail you.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ: that is, with justice and equity. وَصَوَّرَكُمْ فَأَحْسَنَ صُوَرَكُمْ. From Abū Razīn: صَوَّرَكُمْ [read «صِوَرَكُمْ»]: he likened the pattern fuʿla to fiʿla, just as fiʿla is likened to fuʿla. They said: kiswa and kusā, rishwa and rushā, and liḥya and luḥā is more frequent; and they said: quwwa and quwā. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is due to the affinity of the ḍamma with the kasra. وَإِلَيْهِ الْمَصِيرُ: that is, the return of all of you, and He will requite you for your deeds.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: يَعْلَمُ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ: the mīm may be assimilated into the mīm, and likewise وَيَعْلَمُ ما تُسِرُّونَ وَما تُعْلِنُونَ. The meaning is: and He knows what you conceal and what you disclose among yourselves of word and deed. وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِذاتِ الصُّدُورِ: that is, knowing what your breasts hide and what your souls enfold, which is more hidden than the secret.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t:
أَلَمْ يَأْتِكُمْ نَبَأُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ قَبْلُ: the origin is «يأتيكم»; the yāʾ was dropped for the jussive (jazm). Whoever says «ألم يأتِكَ», for him the origin is «يأتيك», and the ḍamma was dropped for the jussive; however, the first is the more eloquent usage. Sībawayh said: Know that when the final letter is quiescent in the nominative, it is dropped in the jussive. Abū Jaʿfar said:
I heard Abū Isḥāq say: we read before Muḥammad ibn Yazīd: "Know that when the final letter is quiescent in the nominative and the genitive, it is dropped in the jussive, so that the jussive should not be the same as the nominative and the genitive". فَذاقُوا وَبالَ أَمْرِهِمْ: that is, the punishment touched them for their disbelief. وَلَهُمْ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ: that is, in the Hereafter.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t:
ذلِكَ بِأَنَّهُ: the hāʾ is an allusion (kināya) to the matter (al-ḥadīth, i.e. the pronoun of the matter), and what follows it explains it and is the khabar (predicate) of "anna". كانَتْ تَأْتِيهِمْ رُسُلُهُمْ بِالْبَيِّناتِ: that is, with the proofs and demonstrations. فَقالُوا أَبَشَرٌ يَهْدُونَنا: He said «يهدوننا» (they guide us), while the word «بشر» is singular. The grammarians discussed the like of this. Some of them said: «يهدوننا» is according to the meaning, and «يهدينا» would be according to the wording. Al-Māzinī spoke — and he mentioned reasons in questions of grammar — among them that the grammarians permitted saying «جاءني ثلاثةُ نفرٍ» and «ثلاثةُ رهطٍ» (three persons came to me), these two being collective nouns, yet did not permit «جاءني ثلاثةُ قومٍ» or «ثلاثةُ بشرٍ», although these two are, according to some grammarians, collective nouns. Al-Māzinī said: «جاءني ثلاثةُ نفرٍ» and «ثلاثةُ رهطٍ» are permitted only because «نفر» and «رهط» are for the smallest numbers, so it fell in its proper place; whereas «بشر» is for a large number and «قوم» for small and large, so for that reason this was not permitted with them. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd disagreed with him in his reasoning about «بشر» and agreed with him in the rest, saying: «بشر» may be for the singular and the plural. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said:
ما هذا بَشَراً [Yūsuf: 31]. He said: for that reason «جاءني ثلاثةُ بشرٍ» is not permitted. فَكَفَرُوا: that is, they denied the prophets of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and His signs. وَتَوَلَّوْا: that is, they turned their backs on faith. وَاسْتَغْنَى اللَّهُ: from their faith. وَاللَّهُ غَنِيٌّ: free of need of all His creation. حَمِيدٌ: that is, praised among them for the favours and bounty of His that they know.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: أَنْ and what follows it stand in place of two objects. قُلْ بَلى وَرَبِّي لَتُبْعَثُنَّ: from your graves. ثُمَّ لَتُنَبَّؤُنَّ بِما عَمِلْتُمْ: that is, you will be informed of it and called to account for it. وَذلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ: that is, easy, because nothing is beyond Him.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: فَآمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَالنُّورِ الَّذِي أَنْزَلْنا: that is, the Qur'an. وَاللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: يَوْمَ يَجْمَعُكُمْ لِيَوْمِ الْجَمْعِ: what governs «يومَ» is «لَتُنَبَّؤُنَّ». The pronoun in «يجمعكم» refers back to the name of Allah; it may not refer back to "the day": if you said «جئتُ يومَ يوافقك» (I came on the day it suits you), it would not be permissible — «يوم» is not put in construct with a verb containing a pronoun referring back to it — for a reason that this is not the place to mention. ذلِكَ يَوْمُ التَّغابُنِ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); outside the Qur'an, «يومَ» in the accusative as an adverb (ẓarf) would be permissible. وَمَنْ يُؤْمِنْ بِاللَّهِ وَيَعْمَلْ صالِحاً: conjoined (maʿṭūf); «ويعملُ» in the nominative would be permissible, as being in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). يُكَفِّرْ عَنْهُ سَيِّئاتِهِ: that is, We erase his evil deeds from him. وَيُدْخِلْهُ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ خالِدِينَ فِيها: accusative as a ḥāl. أَبَداً: as an adverb (ẓarf). ذلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ: a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; and «الفوز» is salvation.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَكَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا: that is, Our proofs and arguments, and [some say] Our Book. وَالَّذِينَ: nominative by being the mubtadaʾ (subject). أُولئِكَ: a second mubtadaʾ. أَصْحابُ النَّارِ: the khabar (predicate) of the second, and the clause is the khabar of «الذين». خالِدِينَ فِيها: as a ḥāl (circumstantial). وَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ: «المصير» is nominative by «بئس»; their destination is the Fire.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t:
ما أَصابَ مِنْ مُصِيبَةٍ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ: «ما» here is negation and has no grammatical position. وَمَنْ يُؤْمِنْ بِاللَّهِ يَهْدِ قَلْبَهُ: ʿIkrima read يَهْدِ قَلْبَهُ with fatḥa on the dāl and «قلبُه» in the nominative, on the basis that its origin is «يهدأ قلبُه», i.e. "is set at rest"; the hamza was replaced by an alif, which was then dropped for the jussive, as the poet said: [al-Ṭawīl] 494-
سريعا وإلّا يبد بالظّلم يظلم
(Swiftly; and if he does not start the wrongdoing, he is wronged.)
وَاللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ: that is, of what has been and of what will be.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: وَأَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ: that is, in what He has commanded you and forbidden you. الرَّسُولَ: conjoined. فَإِنْ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ: that is, if you turn your backs, are too proud to obey him and disobey him. فَإِنَّما عَلى رَسُولِنَا الْبَلاغُ الْمُبِينُ: that is, [his duty is only] to convey, while the reckoning and the punishment belong to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: اللَّهُ لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ: that is, divinity befits none but Him. وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ: a command; the original form is with kasra on the lām.

nahhas-irab:14-14.t: عَدُوًّا: the noun (ism) of «إنّ»; and «عدوّ» may have the meaning of «أعداء» (enemies). It has been said: that is, they command you to sins and forbid you obedience, and this is the severest enmity. فَاحْذَرُوهُمْ: that is, [beware] of accepting from them. وَإِنْ تَعْفُوا: the nūn was dropped for the jussive. وَتَصْفَحُوا: conjoined to it, and likewise وَتَغْفِرُوا; that is: if you pardon what they did in the past, overlook punishing them and forgive their sins apart from that. فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ: that is, [forgiving] to whoever repents; "merciful", i.e. [He does not] punish him after repentance. [Translator's note: the text reads «رحيم أي يعذبه بعد التوبة» "merciful, i.e. He punishes him after repentance"; a negation (لا) appears to have dropped out, and it is rendered here with the negation supplied in brackets.]

nahhas-irab:15-15.t:
َّما أَمْوالُكُمْ وَأَوْلادُكُمْ فِتْنَةٌ [Translator's note: so in the text, beginning with a broken «َّما»; the verse begins إِنَّما.]
Qatāda said: that is, a trial. Ibn Zayd reported from his father, who said: The Prophet ﷺ was giving a sermon when he saw al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn stumbling along, so he came down from the pulpit, held them close to him and recited نَّما أَمْوالُكُمْ وَأَوْلادُكُمْ فِتْنَةٌ [Translator's note: so in the text, again with the beginning of إِنَّما broken.]
Qatāda said: اللَّهُ عِنْدَهُ أَجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ:
that is, Paradise.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t:
فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُمْ: «ما» is in the position of the accusative (naṣb), i.e. "so fear Allah to the extent of what you are able", i.e. to the extent of your ability, like وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ [Yūsuf: 82]. Qatāda's view that this verse abrogates His saying, Mighty and Majestic: اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ تُقاتِهِ [Āl ʿImrān: 102] is a view that is not sound; abrogating and abrogated (al-nāsikh wa-l-mansūkh) are established only by authoritative instruction (tawqīf) or by establishing a decisive proof. The two verses agree, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not impose what is beyond ability. So the meaning of "fear Allah as He should be feared" is: in what you are able. وَاسْمَعُوا: that is, what you are commanded. وَأَطِيعُوا وَأَنْفِقُوا خَيْراً لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ: concerning the accusative of «خيرا» there are four views. The view of Sībawayh is that the meaning is "and bring about good for yourselves". It has been said: the meaning is "it will be good for yourselves". The third view: "a spending that is good for yourselves". The fourth view is that you put «خيرا» in the accusative by «أنفقوا» (spend), «الخير» being wealth. وَمَنْ يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفْسِهِ: al-Farrāʾ reported that it was read «ومن يوقَ شِحَّ نفسه» with kasra on the shīn, and this is anomalous (shādhdh).
فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ: that is, those who have attained what they sought.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: إِنْ تُقْرِضُوا اللَّهَ قَرْضاً حَسَناً: that is, by your spending in His way. يُضاعِفْهُ لَكُمْ: the apodosis (mujāzāh). وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ: conjoined; it may be nominative by being cut off from the first, and accusative by «الصرف» (deflection). وَاللَّهُ شَكُورٌ حَلِيمٌ: that is, He thanks whoever spends in His way, and the meaning of His thanking him is His rewarding him and accepting his deed. حَلِيمٌ: in refraining from punishment in this world.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: It is possible that الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ is a naʿt (adjective) of the name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and that «عالمُ الغيب» is a second khabar (predicate), or a naʿt if it has the sense of the past, because it is then definite. It is also possible that all of it is a badal (substitute), because a definite may be substituted for an indefinite.
